alerts.reason: Reported annual sales fell 2%, and lower sales and production volumes weighed on earnings (B, E). Aerospace and defense sales still grew in the Americas and EMEA, while weaker Chinese activity reduced Asia Pacific sales (A). I forecast those regional gains keep the September-quarter sales change above -5%, with continued volume pressure pushing the December-quarter change to -5% or worse.

Records A and B imply March-quarter sales grew about 16% year over year before June-quarter sales fell 3.6%. Work Truck Solutions gained volume and pricing, while low snowfall cut attachment volumes (C, D). I expect Solutions to cushion September sales, then weaker attachment demand to push the consolidated December-quarter decline to at least 5%.

June net sales fell 1.8% as NN reduced volume at plants undergoing turnarounds. Contractual pricing partly offset the volume reductions and a $1.0 million currency headwind (A). I forecast pricing keeps the September decline under 5%, but further plant volume reductions widen the December decline to at least 5%.

June sales fell just 1.3%, but the order backlog fell 22.9% year over year, from $688.8 million to $531.1 million (A, C). I expect existing orders to keep September's sales decline under 5%, with fewer orders left to ship by December pushing the decline to at least 5%.

June net sales rose 2.9% as component availability improved and Tennant shipped against its backlog. The backlog fell from $186.2 million in December to $110.0 million in June (A–C). I expect remaining orders to keep September sales growth above -5%, then diminishing backlog shipments and weaker EMEA and APAC sales (D) to push December growth to -5% or worse.

Cerence accelerated $67.8 million of deferred revenue into fiscal Q1 2024 (C), raising the prior-year comparison specifically for the quarter beginning in October. June revenue grew 14.4% (A). I forecast September growth above -5%, followed by a December decline of at least 5% as Cerence compares against that accelerated revenue.

Schneider's consolidated June revenue fell about 2%. Logistics revenue excluding fuel surcharges fell $24.6 million as both brokerage volume and revenue per order declined (A, B). I forecast a September consolidated decline under 5%, widening to at least 5% in December as fewer orders at lower rates compound the shortfall.
